tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on symptom/user-intent triggers (patching failures, errors, hangs) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly lists trigger contexts including when the user doesn't name the service, and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Windows Server EC2 instance's patching is blocked by a Windows update service or runtime fault rather than component-store corruption. ... including when the user only says patching "won't start" or "hangs" without naming a service.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific identifiers (error codes, service names, registry paths, DLLs) without explaining general concepts the agent would already know. It is dense and non-redundant.
tests.evidence: wuauserv Disabled (0x80070422, StartType: Disabled): SSM can start a Stopped/Manual service but cannot start a Disabled one.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, exact operations (service re-enable commands, GAC re-registration, snapshotting first) are given precise commands, while diagnosis/routing steps explain reasoning (e.g., 'the GPO is the real fix') rather than being rigidly prescriptive where flexibility is fine.
tests.evidence: Re-enable it (Set-Service -StartupType Automatic) then start — and note a GPO may re-disable it on the next refresh.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Each fault type maps to one clear fix path (e.g., gacutil /i for AWSSDK.Core, msiexec /unregister then /regserver for MSI) rather than listing multiple equal alternative tools.
tests.evidence: Re-register AWSSDK.Core.dll into the GAC with gacutil /i (snapshot first).

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic/routing/recovery/validation procedure applicable to any instance hitting these fault classes, not a one-off declaration for a specific instance.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the service/runtime fault before acting... Step 2: Route to the fault (load the matching reference)

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Gotchas section provides concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to this Windows patching domain (Disabled vs Stopped, GPO re-disable timing, GAC/AV exclusion, DataStore.edb caution).
tests.evidence: Disabled ≠ Stopped. SSM/patch baseline can start a Stopped/Manual service but not a Disabled one
